summary: Creates or reinitializes a session structure. Lazily allocates an 849-byte buffer into dword_5E64F4 when it is null, clears its first byte, and calls a setup routine with a session-flag argument. Then iterates a subsystem setup table from off_5E6500 to off_5E6530 in three-entry steps, appending a ";" delimiter and calling a compare routine on each table entry; a matching entry clears the match flag. When a match occurred the session buffer is returned; otherwise the buffer is torn down, dword_5E64F4 cleared to 0, and the fallback pointer off_5E650C returned. Called by sub_588A34.

local_names.v1: match flag: 1 until a table entry matches
local_names.v2: table iterator advancing three entries per step
local_names.v3: entry base pointer used for the compare
local_names.v5: compare value loaded from the table entry three slots ahead

operations.description: If dword_5E64F4 is null, lazily allocate the 849-byte session buffer with MallocWrapperForNhMalloc and store it back into dword_5E64F4.
Clear the first byte of the session buffer.
BatchFunctionCallOverVarargs(dword_5E64F4, 3) performs the initial session setup call.
Iterate the subsystem setup table from off_5E6500 to off_5E6530, advancing three pointer entries (12 bytes) per step.
sub_58FCB0(dword_5E64F4, ";") appends the ";" delimiter to the session buffer.
Load compare value v5 from the table entry three slots ahead (v2[3]).
sub_58FB90(*v3, v5) compares the current table entry against the loaded value; a non-zero result clears the match flag v1.
BatchFunctionCallOverVarargs(dword_5E64F4, 3) runs the setup routine on each iteration.
If the match flag v1 stayed set (no table entry matched), fall through to teardown; otherwise return the session buffer.
sub_58AA6F(dword_5E64F4) tears down the session buffer, then dword_5E64F4 is cleared to 0.
Return the session buffer on match, otherwise the fallback pointer off_5E650C.
